claims.harm: unsolicited modification of consensus rules without user demand or emergent consensus
claims.quote: this proposal represents an unsolicited modification of Bitcoin’s code and consensus rules. There is no clear user demand, no demonstrated market need, and no compelling application that justifies taking on this risk.

claims.harm: risk of contentious chain split without clear user demand and community consensus
claims.quote: Any proposed change should be weighed against the worst-case scenario: civil war or a chain split, which we’ve seen before.

claims.harm: merging consensus rules into Core before rough community consensus sets a bad precedent and dictates rules
claims.quote: As this introduces a new consensus feature, it seems premature to merge this into Bitcoin Core until widespread consensus is reached among Bitcoin users to eventually activate this new feature in a soft fork.

claims.harm: merging into Core acts as a step toward an activation attempt causing a potential chain split
claims.quote: Merging this pull request would be a step towards a second declared activation attempt for CTV and a potential chain split if there isn't community consensus.

claims.harm: zero functional consensus test coverage without defining a regtest deployment
claims.quote: Currently there is zero consensus coverage at the functional level from what I can tell

claims.harm: cheap DoS vector where peers repeatedly broadcast max-block-weight CTV spends by tweaking 1 bit to force re-hashing
claims.quote: What prevents a peer to repeat broadcast of such ~MAX_BLOCK_WEIGHT tx CTV-spend to a target node ? Peer cost is just to tweaking some random 1-bit in the whole ~MAX_BLOCK_WEIGHT surface.

claims.harm: legacy script deployment is exposed to block sigop overflow attacks that break time-sensitive contracts, unlike Taproot OP_SUCCESS
claims.quote: I think it would be valuable to have CTV rather as a taproot op_success.
claims.settled_by_quote: I would support a change of CTV to be Taproot only, but I also understand the concern of the champions with the realities of the bitcoin ecosystem, where most of the coins spents are Segwit V0.

support.reason: CTV is an objectively well-reviewed, fundamental upgrade to Bitcoin with broad consensus among subject matter experts, providing scaling techniques without fundamentally altering Bitcoin
simple implementation, helpful comments, good test coverage, no backwards compatibility issues, passes all CI
Concept ACK. There are a few things that look like rebase leftovers that are added and removed in the different commits.
Reviewed, code seems correct and to match the old prs closely.
Strongly support getting this in Regtest and Signet and doing further battle testing
finds CTV desirable for condensing mining pool coinbase payouts to self-custodial addresses by deferring block space consumption
minimal extension of script capabilities allowing immutable vertices in transaction graphs useful for off-chain protocol designers
